title: Add resilient instrumentation + fallback for stranded span indexes and missing metrics
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted and Dedicated tiers reported dashboards showing intermittent blank tiles and missing metric series during a recent autoscaler rollout. Investigation shows a race in the trace index compaction + eviction path where compacted index segments were marked as deleted before background re-index jobs finished writing KV pointers. Symptoms: stale trace links from console tiles, missing time-series for short windows, and N+1 gaps in span stitching for long-running requests.

Root cause: index-compaction worker triggered by autoscaler-related load spikes removes segment manifests in the trace index while the re-indexing job (async backfill) still holds transient pointers. This leads to two outcomes: 1) span-to-metric stitching fails because the span index lookup returns 404 for segments the backfill expected to exist, and 2) dashboard live panels query the metric index and get an empty series for certain short windows. The core bug is a lack of a safe handoff and a missing fallback read path when index pointers are transiently absent.

Goal: implement a resilient read fallback and safe compaction handshake to prevent customer-impacting blank tiles and tracing gaps, plus an emergency backfill playbook to recover any affected tenants. The fix must be compatible with Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments and avoid excessive read amplification or CPU spikes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Console trace links and dashboard tiles no longer return blank/empty during compaction events in a staged rollout (canary -> full).
- Automated tests that simulate compaction+backfill race and verify fallback path returns best-effort spans/metrics.
- Backfill runbook and one-click remediation script validated on staging and used for two impacted tenants.
- No measurable >5% increase in median read latency across tenant reads in normal traffic after the fallback enabled.

Planned work:
1) Add conservative read-fallback: when a trace index lookup misses, perform a bounded search against recent compacted segment manifests and the KV cache (prefers cached pointers) before returning empty. This should be rate-limited per-tenant to avoid amplification.
2) Implement compaction handshake: compaction worker marks segment state as "quiescing", waits for in-flight backfill leases to release (lease manager), then atomically swaps manifests to remove segments.
3) Add metrics and alerts: compaction-handshake-failures, fallback-read-rate, fallback-success-rate, tenant-affected-count.
4) Backfill tooling: one-off reindex job that scans recent traces and rebuilds missing pointers + a safe throttling policy.
5) Staged rollout and canary on a subset of tenants (hosted dev orgs, 3 dedicated customers).

Telemetry to watch during rollout:
- Dashboard blank-tile rate (console-empty-tile-5m)
- Span-stitch-failure-rate (stitch.failure.rate-5m)
- Compaction-handshake-duration histogram
- Fallback-read-invocations and success ratio
- Read P50/P95 latency for trace lookups

Backward compatibility and deploy constraints:
- Private deployments: provide migration migration-guide and a toggle to enable handshake/fallback. Must avoid attempting aggressive background reads on air-gapped clusters.
- Dedicated: coordinate with account owners for maintenance window if we need heavy backfill.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: fallback reads increase read load and could surface noisy-neighbor issues. Mitigation: per-tenant rate limits and exponential backoff on fallback path.
- Risk: handshake introduces latency to compaction. Mitigation: handshake uses short leases (<= 30s) and metrics to monitor compaction tail latency.
- Risk: backfill could cause storage I/O spikes. Mitigation: throttled reindex with I/O budget and run during off-peak hours per region.

Runbook links and artifacts:
- Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/1247
- Backfill job: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/backfills/trace-pointer-reindex
- Incident postmortem (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/2026-02-21+Trace+Index+Compaction+Incident
- Customer notifications: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1abc-example-notice/edit

Rollout plan:
- 2026-03-12: Merge feature-flagged code to staging, run simulated compaction race tests.
- 2026-03-15: Canary enable for 5% of hosted traffic and two dedicated customers; monitor key telemetry for 48h.
- 2026-03-18: Gradual ramp to 50% if no regression.
- 2026-03-20: Full rollout and run backfill for affected tenants.

Notes: ensure console team is on-call during canary windows and that support templates are prepared for customers asking for status updates.
